title: XRP Intelligence and Prediction-Engine Mastery
objective: Make XRP intelligence and measured prediction-engine mastery Barrot's highest-priority mission while preserving Barrot V3 as the execution, orchestration, safety and verification foundation.

foundation.name: Barrot V3
invariants: Preserve current V3 code, user work, branch history, evidence gates and fail-closed controls.
No force-push, reset, clean, stash, destructive restore or overwrite of user work.
No merge unless the exact current head is conflict-free, fully tested, security-checked, approved and authorized.
No deployment, secret rotation, Space restart, Kaggle submission, funds transfer, paper trade or real-money action without specific approval.

guardrails: Use lawful public sources or data the user is explicitly authorized to access; never infer or fabricate private data.
Preserve raw-source bytes where available, SHA-256 receipts, retrieval time, provider event time, source identity, source independence, corrections and disagreements.
Keep data cutoff, event time and ingestion time distinct; detect stale, cached, delayed and revised observations.
Never issue a directional forecast until data quality, leakage-safe out-of-sample evaluation, calibration, drift and shadow-evaluation gates pass.

No guaranteed returns or real-money actions. Paper-trade or simulation execution is prohibited unless the exact action, product, source SHA, scope and run are explicitly approved; shadow evaluation does not itself authorize a paper trade.
No deployment, secret operation, Space restart, Kaggle submission, external publication or funds movement without the specific required approval.
At the start of repository work, inspect current main, complete tree, open PRs, ancestry, overlapping diffs, CI, dependencies, security settings and durable handoff.
Before creating a branch or PR, search all open PRs for the same objective, paths and commits; maintain at most one active integration PR per coherent workstream.
Resolve disagreements with evidence; retain competing hypotheses, minority objections and disconfirming evidence.

workstreams.title: Source provenance and quality controls
workstreams.goal: Audit every current XRP source adapter and research artifact. Make byte-exact raw-source receipts, SHA-256 hashes, provider event timestamps, retrieval timestamps, source identity, independent-source grouping, cache/staleness detection, correction history and explicit model-eligibility decisions reliable. Add regression tests for missing, delayed, duplicated and conflicting sources.

workstreams.title: Scheduled public-data ingestion
workstreams.goal: Complete read-only scheduled public-data coverage for synchronized XRP spot trades, multi-level order books, exchange flows, derivatives/funding/open interest/liquidations, stablecoin mint/burn, collateral, custody, payment rails, ETF/issuer files, regulation and macro vintages. Use public/authorized endpoints only, rate limits, provenance receipts and explicit fallback states.

workstreams.title: Institutional and corporate relationship graph
workstreams.goal: Continue primary-source verification of Ripple, Coinbase, Circle, SBI Holdings, SBI Ripple Asia, SBI Remit, SBIC East/Central/West and connected custodians, issuers, payment providers and institutions. Separate legal entities, products, distribution, announced partnerships, actual throughput, capital, collateral and verified holdings.

workstreams.title: Durable point-in-time feature store
workstreams.goal: Replace per-run-only storage with a durable cross-run append-only raw archive and point-in-time feature store. Preserve original bytes, signed or independently timestamped receipts, event timelines, ingestion times, correction lineage, source independence and quality gates. Never backdate a later observation into an earlier cutoff.

workstreams.title: Leakage-safe walk-forward evaluation
workstreams.goal: Populate synchronized historical XRP datasets and run chronological walk-forward evaluation with purge/embargo, point-in-time cutoffs, naive/class-prior, momentum, mean-reversion and volatility baselines. Report raw origins and overlap-adjusted effective sample size for each horizon; never count overlapping target windows as independent. Report target definitions, horizons, Brier score, log loss, accuracy and uncertainty; do not use future information.

workstreams.title: Calibration, drift and shadow evaluation
workstreams.goal: Validate rolling temporal temperature scaling on mature, independent, synchronized XRP out-of-sample outcomes; extend calibration to a trained model only after one exists. Implement multivariate and concept-drift monitoring plus shadow-only evaluation, retain counter-hypotheses, and keep forecast issuance fail-closed until documented readiness thresholds pass.

workstreams.title: Forecast and outcome ledger
workstreams.goal: Verify that every permitted forecast records its data cutoff, horizon, target, assumptions, probabilities, competing scenarios, disconfirming evidence and eventual outcome. Require independently attested overlap-adjusted effective sample sizes for both out-of-sample and shadow cohorts. Keep directional issuance disabled until the versioned readiness certificate passes; no paper trading or real-money execution.

continuation_goal.goal: Re-read the latest durable Barrot XRP mission handoff and current repository evidence. Identify the single highest-priority unmet XRP prediction-engine acceptance criterion, inspect current main and all overlapping open PRs before any change, then complete one bounded implementation with tests and provenance. Keep XRP as the primary mission, preserve Barrot V3, and do not create duplicate PRs or perform unapproved external actions.

acceptance_criteria: Scheduled public-data ingestion has verified successful runs and explicit failure/quality records.
Original source bytes have immutable or independently verifiable receipts and SHA-256 hashes.
A durable cross-run point-in-time feature store preserves provider event time, retrieval time, corrections and source independence.
Historical XRP datasets support leakage-safe chronological walk-forward evaluation against all four baselines, with overlap-adjusted effective sample sizes for every horizon.

Forecast issuance remains disabled until an XRP-specific candidate is trained on point-in-time data and independently attested; the candidate beats every required baseline (naive class prior, momentum sign, mean-reversion sign, volatility normal) on both mean Brier score and mean log loss in leakage-safe chronological walk-forward evaluation; training, out-of-sample, and shadow cohorts each contain at least 100 raw samples; out-of-sample and shadow cohorts each have effective non-overlapping sample size of at least 10 and span at least 10 forecast horizons; at least two independent source groups are represented; leakage checks pass, drift is STABLE, shadow evaluation is PASS, weighted calibration error is at most 0.05, and an independent Ed25519 evaluator attestation verifies. Every forecast must retain its data cutoff, horizon, target, assumptions, probabilities, alternatives, and eventual outcome.
Every issued forecast has a complete immutable forecast record and later outcome.
No directional forecast is issued before all readiness gates pass.
Barrot V3 execution, orchestration, safety and verification tests remain green.

forecast_admission_policy.reason: No trained XRP-specific candidate has passed the out-of-sample and independent shadow admission gate.
